leadHtml: Rated by current use, not by level. HOT is in daily use. WARM is current but not in active use. COLD is archived.

rows.p: Moodle core internals, every plugin type, upgrade paths, Behat and PHPUnit, theme layers, DB portability across MySQL and PostgreSQL.
Nine years. Plugin architecture, hook layers, and keeping plugin code thin enough to survive a core release.
JavaScript, Mustache, SCSS, accessibility, and theme maintenance across Moodle upgrades.
Rust, Node services, Linux and systemd units, Docker, Wayland, and local speech recognition and synthesis, all on a single machine.
Tool-using agent systems, headless runners on systemd timers, audit logging, and non-chat interfaces for agents.
Distillation and compression experiments on consumer hardware. Graph networks and pruning schedules.
Linear algebra, Fourier analysis, and the probability required for model work.
Electronic Engineering, embedded work, robotics. Unused since university.

method.p: Work starts from a written definition of done, agreed before any code is written.
The smallest change that solves the stated problem. No speculative abstraction.
Projects that no longer justify their cost are marked retired and closed out.
Every project note records what was tried, what failed, and any prior work that reached the result first.

explored.p: I built an ARC-AGI solving toolkit: a grid DSL, a Tkinter interface for hand-composing solutions as DSL programs, and a fine-tuning pipeline (PEFT on a small Gemma, a visual FAISS index) over the solved examples — Python, numpy, PyTorch, transformers.
I built a data-ingestion and reporting platform for a public waste-management agency: Django, PostgreSQL, MinIO object storage, Apache NiFi flows, Docker Compose.

I explored graph-shaped neural networks that learn with local Hebbian rules instead of backprop, and that prune themselves during a sleep phase — Fibonacci versus random wiring, product neurons, wake/sleep cycles — in Python/PyTorch with a Rust wiring simulator.
I built a Godot 4 framework that gives LLM agents a body in a 2D top-down world, with an emotion engine and agent-to-agent talk over the Google A2A protocol — GDScript, MCP, Hermes/OpenClaw gateways.

I explored transformers as linear operators from a DSP angle: impulse-response probing of the residual stream, spectral truncation, and knowledge distillation of GPT-2 into a small student using noise as the excitation signal — PyTorch, TransformerLens, ROCm.

I explored mechanistic understanding of CNNs, LLMs and GNNs and of quantum algorithms through a predict-first question protocol, with a SvelteKit playground whose librarian runs on the Claude Agent SDK.
I explored agent orchestration and prompt engineering with the Hermes agent framework and MCP.
I explored transformer internals, training dynamics and mechanistic interpretability through a build-from-scratch study plan in JAX and PyTorch.
I explored quantum machine learning: a from-scratch numpy quantum kernel SVM audited against a classical RBF kernel, plus a React/TypeScript study console for the linear-algebra groundwork.
